preceding_messages.speaker: Y
preceding_messages.text: I adopt the semiannual re-survey cadence, the five-degree obstruction threshold, the NOAA-residual bias-term estimation, and the 1.0 °C relocation-review trigger verbatim; they convert the larch-canopy failure from a nine-week invisible ramp into a flagged, correctable, auditable entry. The four-week residual regression your correction line depends on, however, is itself vulnerable to contamination: if the NOAA comparison station underwent a site migration, instrument replacement, or published a quality-control exclusion during those four weeks, the residual conflates the neighbour's shade bias with the comparison station's own discontinuity and attributes the latter to the microclimate term, netting in a correction that compensates the wrong artifact. I therefore mandate that before any correction line is executed the compiler must verify, from the NOAA station's published metadata record, that no site-migration flag, instrument-replacement entry, or quality-control exclusion falls inside the four-week estimation window; if any such flag is present the correction line is deferred and the affected comparison cells print "NOAA DISCONTINUITY — CORRECTION DEFERRED" rather than a populated bias term, so a year-two appendix auditor never mistakes a comparison-station artifact for a neighbourhood-scale microclimate shift.

preceding_messages.speaker: X
preceding_messages.text: I adopt the NOAA-metadata verification gate and the "NOAA DISCONTINUITY — CORRECTION DEFERRED" annotation verbatim. Because that gate catches only formally logged events, I further mandate a sliding-window coherence check on the NOAA comparison column itself: any rolling eight-week cumulative drift exceeding ±0.4 °C—roughly the signature of an unflagged 0.05 °C/week thermistor creep—invalidates the four-week estimation window and defers the correction line under the same annotation. The failure this closes is that the NOAA station four kilometres east accumulates a silent +0.1 °C/week thermistor drift over six weeks with no replacement entry in its metadata, the compiler's weeks 3–6 window absorbs +0.4 °C of that drift, freezes a spurious +1.0 °C microclimate bias term into the neighborhood site, and suppresses every subsequent comparison cell by that amount, so that a genuine October larch-canopy-closure cooling of 1.2 °C reads as only −0.2 °C and vanishes below the ±0.5 °C weekly tolerance. Any week in which the eight-week coherence check trips therefore prints "NOAA DRIFT — CORRECTION DEFERRED" in the affected comparison cell, with the deferred correction queued for re-estimation once a clean four-week window resumes.

target.speaker: Y
target.text: I adopt the eight-week cumulative-drift coherence check, the ±0.4 °C threshold, the "NOAA DRIFT — CORRECTION DEFERRED" annotation, and the queued re-estimation rule verbatim; they close the silent-thermistor-creep hole at the estimation-window level rather than at the individual-reading level. The gap your coherence check implies but your existing two-initials erratum protocol does not cover is the retrospective invalidation of a correction line already executed during a window later revealed contaminated: I mandate that when the eight-week drift metric trips in week N and defers a microclimate correction applied in the preceding window, the subsequent bulletin's appendix prints a single "RETROACTIVE DEFERRAL" note keyed to the correction-line serial identifying which prior weeks' comparison cells are now suspect, and those cells in all future bulletins revert to "NOAA DRIFT — CORRECTION DEFERRED" until a clean four-week window resumes, but no superseding bulletin is issued for the already-printed copies because the correction was statistically valid at its moment of execution. The failure this distinguishes from a full erratum cascade: if the compiler silently re-issues six consecutive bulletins with struck-through comparison cells under the two-initials protocol for what was a legitimate-at-the-time microclimate correction, a volunteer observer reading the year-one appendix sees a week-long cascade of invalidated comparison cells and reads the institution as systematically corrupt rather than as statistically conservative, stripping the project of the public-credibility anchor your transcription-slip rule was designed to preserve.
